market_rationale: Stagflationary macro: CPI 3.7% with energy +5.2%, PPI 6.3%, Fed hiking to 3.75-4.00% with FOMC on Oct 27-28, Brent $113, 10y near 5%. Mega-cap tech and semis sold off sharply (Nasdaq -2.6% on Oct 22) while breadth was positive (two-thirds of S&P up, RSP beating SPY by 3.8% over 21 sessions). This is a rotation from crowded AI/semis leadership to equal-weight, value, and defensives rather than a broad risk-off. Shock-reversal candidates with strong prior trends (Taiwan, semis, Korea) deserve a reversal test, but the rate and inflation backdrop is a headwind for high-beta duration-like growth, so only the highest-quality pullbacks get modest overreaction credit. Equal-weight/value and energy have in-window macro support.
portfolio_rationale: Only Taiwan clears the overreaction and 55% bar: strong prior trend, moderate drawdown, high quality score, pullback without volume capitulation. Equal-weight S&P is a supported continuation on broad breadth and rotation out of mega-cap tech but is not an overreaction label. AI tech and semis get reversal tests but the hiking Fed, 10y near 5%, and the Oct 27-28 FOMC plus Nov 10 CPI keep their edge near coin-flip, so most of the portfolio defaults to SPY. Commodity-linked losers (silver, metals) show deterioration rather than overreaction; oil and Brazil are extended without an independent in-window edge beyond geopolitics already priced.
